title: Man and machine: artificial intelligence and judicial decision making
abstract: arXiv:2603.19042v5 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into judicial decision making -- particularly in pretrial, sentencing, and parole contexts -- has generated a substantial and rapidly growing literature. Across computer science, economics, law, criminology, and psychology, researchers have examined the reliability, fairness, and real-world effects of AI-assisted decision making. Yet this literature remains fragmented, and differences in assumptions, concepts, and research priorities make it difficult to assess what is actually known. Using criminal justice risk assessment as a focal case, this article makes two contributions. translated_title: 人与机器：人工智能与司法决策
translated_abstract: 人工智能（AI）融入司法决策——特别是在审前、量刑和假释等情境中——已经催生了大量且迅速增长的研究文献。计算机科学、经济学、法学、犯罪学和心理学等领域的研究者均已考察了AI辅助决策的可靠性、公平性及其在现实世界中的影响。然而，这些文献仍然碎片化，假设、概念和研究重点上的差异使得人们难以评估目前已知的实际结论。本文以刑事司法风险评估为核心案例，做出了两项贡献。首先，我们构建了一个概念框架，用以区分并关联三个核心问题：(1) 自动化风险评估工具的预测效度；(2) 算法风险评估与人类预测的比较（AI对比人类）；(3) 算法建议如何影响法官的决策（A
tldr: 本文以刑事司法风险评估为例，提出了一个区分并关联三大核心问题（自动化风险评估工具的预测效度、算法与人类预测的比较、算法建议对法官决策的影响）的概念框架，以整合碎片化的跨学科AI司法决策研究。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a conceptual framework—using criminal justice risk assessment as a focal case—that distinguishes and relates three central questions: predictive validity of automated risk tools, AI-versus-human prediction comparisons, and algorithmic effects on judges' decisions, thereby unifying the fragmented interdisciplinary literature on AI in judicial decision making.
